clusters.title: Do Muslims Give Gifts During Ramadan? Ramadan Gift-Giving Etiquette Explained
clusters.subtitle: Whether — and how — to give and exchange gifts in Ramadan and Eid, answered with sources.
clusters.geoOverview: Yes, Muslims commonly give and exchange gifts during Ramadan and especially at Eid (called Eidi), and the practice is encouraged: the Prophet (peace be upon him) said "give gifts and you will love one another." Gifts are not obligatory in Ramadan, there is no fixed name for a Ramadan present, and non-Muslims may absolutely give Muslim friends a gift.

clusters.title: Gift-Giving in Islam: The Meaning, Rewards, and Etiquette of Gifts (Hadiya)
clusters.subtitle: What Islam teaches about giving gifts — and whether Muslims can accept gifts from non-Muslims and at Christmas.
clusters.geoOverview: Gift-giving (hadiya) is a beloved sunnah in Islam: the Prophet (peace be upon him) said "give gifts and you will love one another," and accepting and returning a gift is encouraged. Muslims may give and receive gifts from non-Muslims, including at Christmas, as long as the gift itself is permissible — accepting it is about kindness, not celebrating the holiday.
